Density-independent and density-dependent niche breadth

Source: R/niche_breadth.R
niche_breadth.Rd

Fits isodars (unless given fitted ones) and returns, for each species, the density-independent (DI) and density-dependent (DD) niche breadth with bootstrap confidence intervals, the spillover abundance, preference reversals and diagnostic flags. With a species column, everything runs per species and the result has one row per species; otherwise the data are one species.

Usage

niche_breadth(
  fit_or_data,
  ...,
  dependent_at = "asymptote",
  min_occupancy = 1,
  reference_effort = NULL,
  absent = "auto",
  n_boot = 999,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  scaled = TRUE,
  weights = "1/var",
  diagnostics = list(),
  seed = NULL,
  max_search = 10000
)

Arguments

fit_or_data

Data in long or wide format (see fit_isodars()), or the long-format output of fit_isodars() (an isodar_fits table).

...

Passed to fit_isodars() when fit_or_data is data: the column names (species, site, habitat, abundance, effort) or hab_cols, and dim, ndim_method, flip_intercept, absent_max_count, absent_min_sites.

dependent_at

"asymptote", "max_observed" or a total abundance; see Details.

min_occupancy

Individuals required in every used habitat at the spillover abundance.

reference_effort, absent

Passed to fit_isodars() (data only).

n_boot

Number of bootstrap replicates (0 for none).

conf_level

Confidence level of the bootstrap intervals.

scaled

If TRUE, niche breadth is scaled to 0-1 (see iai()).

weights

Pairwise isodars only: "1/var" (default, as in the paper) or NULL; see iai().

diagnostics

Named list of thresholds for the flags; see Details.

seed

Optional random-number seed (bootstrap and null model). Each species then gets its own random streams, so its results do not depend on n_boot or on the other species; your random-number state is restored afterwards.

max_search

Largest total searched for the spillover abundance.

Value

A tibble of class niche_breadth, one row per species, with species (if given), method, n_sites, nb_di, nb_di_lower, nb_di_upper, spillover_abundance, spillover_lower, spillover_upper, nb_dd, nb_dd_lower, nb_dd_upper, dependent_at (Inf for the asymptote), var_explained (line, "pca" only), intercept_p, absent and abandoned (habitats, comma-separated), reversals (list of data frames: total_abundance, habitat_1 (more abundant before), habitat_2, niche_breadth), n_boot_valid, flags (names of the flags raised, comma-separated), one logical flag_* column per diagnostic, and note. Printing it adds one line giving the number of flagged species.

Details

Niche breadth is the isodar-adjusted inequality (iai()): total abundance is allocated among habitats as the isodars predict and niche breadth is 1 - Gini of that allocation (scaled to 0-1 by default). Absent habitats count as 0 (see fit_isodars()).

Spillover abundance \(T_0\) is the smallest total abundance (an integer, in individuals per reference effort; see fit_isodars()) at which every used habitat holds at least min_occupancy individuals: the point at which the species starts to spill over into its least-favoured used habitat. DI niche breadth is the value at \(T_0\). It depends on the sampling unit (reference_effort); DD niche breadth does not.

DD niche breadth. With dependent_at = "asymptote" (default) it is the limit as total abundance \(T \to \infty\), where the allocation is proportional to the direction of the isodar line (or follows the pairwise slopes) and intercepts no longer matter; it is computed directly. A number gives the value at that total, and "max_observed" the value at the largest site total in the data.

The curve between them. If no two habitats change rank and no habitat is abandoned anywhere above \(T_0\) (no reversal or abandoned flag), niche breadth follows $$NB(T) = NB_{DD} + (NB_{DI} - NB_{DD}) T_0 / T,$$ and is halfway between the two values at \(T = 2 T_0\). Otherwise it has this form only piecewise, with different constants between successive reversals. Where the predicted abundances of two habitats cross, the ranking of habitats changes and the curve can be non-monotonic; these preference-reversal abundances are returned in reversals (totals from \(T_0\) upward) and flagged. A habitat used at low density whose predicted abundance falls to 0 at high totals is listed in abandoned (it still counts for DI niche breadth). Use iai_curve() to compute and plot whole curves.

Bootstrap. Whole sites are resampled with replacement and the isodars refitted, keeping the absent habitats (and the line method) of the full data. Intervals are percentile intervals.

Diagnostics. Each flag_* column is TRUE when:

  • few_sites: fewer than min_sites sites;

  • few_pair_sites: some pair of used habitats shares fewer than min_pair_sites sites;

  • low_abundance: the median site total is below min_median_count individuals (counts, not densities), or more than max_zero_share of the sampled cells of used habitats are zeros;

  • di_extrapolation: \(T_0\) lies outside the observed range of site totals by more than a factor extrapolation_ratio;

  • dd_extrapolation: for the asymptote, the largest site total is below extrapolation_ratio x \(T_0\) (with the default 2, the data do not reach the halfway point of the curve); for a numeric dependent_at, it exceeds the largest site total by more than that factor;

  • abandoned: some used habitat is abandoned at high density (informational);

  • reversal: habitats change rank along the curve (informational);

  • poor_fit: the line explains less than min_var_explained of the variance (ndim_method = "pca"), or the pairwise isodars are inconsistent: for some three habitats \(i, j, k\) the slopes \(b_{ij} b_{jk}\) and \(b_{ik}\) differ in sign or by more than a factor max_slope_ratio;

  • disconnected: habitats are not connected through shared sites;

  • intercept_noise: no isodar intercept differs from those expected from sampling alone. Following the paper (section 1.2.3), n_null data sets are simulated without density-dependent habitat selection: each site's individuals are redistributed among its sampled habitats in proportion to the species' overall density in each habitat (multinomial). Two-sided p-values of the pairwise TLS intercepts are Holm-corrected within species; intercept_p is the smallest, and the flag is set when it exceeds alpha. The test needs integer counts (NA otherwise). Set n_null = 0 to skip it;

  • unstable_bootstrap: more than max_failed_share of bootstrap replicates failed, or a confidence interval is wider than max_ci_width;

  • undersampled: a habitat had no records at too few sites to be declared absent (see fit_isodars());

  • no_di: no total up to max_search occupies every used habitat;

  • fit_failed: the isodars could not be fitted (see note).

Defaults: min_sites = 10, min_pair_sites = 5, min_median_count = 5, max_zero_share = 0.5, extrapolation_ratio = 2, min_var_explained = 0.5, max_slope_ratio = 2, n_null = 199, alpha = 0.05, max_failed_share = 0.1, max_ci_width = 0.5. Change any of them through diagnostics, e.g. diagnostics = list(min_sites = 8).

Comparing species. Absent habitats lower niche breadth, so species compared with each other should be assessed over the same set of habitats: the habitats available to them.

See also

iai_curve(), fit_isodars(), check_coverage()

Examples

three <- moorea_fish[moorea_fish$species %in% c("Acanthurus nigrofuscus",
  "Scarus schlegeli", "Siganus argenteus"), ]
nb <- niche_breadth(three, species = "species", site = "site",
                    habitat = "habitat", abundance = "abundance",
                    n_boot = 99, seed = 1)
nb
#> # A tibble: 3 × 35
#>   species       method n_sites nb_di nb_di_lower nb_di_upper spillover_abundance
#>   <chr>         <chr>    <int> <dbl>       <dbl>       <dbl>               <dbl>
#> 1 Acanthurus n… pairw…      13 0.468      0.0668       0.511                 133
#> 2 Scarus schle… pairw…      13 0.143      0.0510       0.574                  30
#> 3 Siganus arge… pairw…      13 0.159      0.0504       0.626                  42
#> # ℹ 28 more variables: spillover_lower <dbl>, spillover_upper <dbl>,
#> #   nb_dd <dbl>, nb_dd_lower <dbl>, nb_dd_upper <dbl>, dependent_at <dbl>,
#> #   var_explained <dbl>, intercept_p <dbl>, absent <chr>, abandoned <chr>,
#> #   reversals <list>, n_boot_valid <int>, flags <chr>, flag_few_sites <lgl>,
#> #   flag_few_pair_sites <lgl>, flag_low_abundance <lgl>,
#> #   flag_di_extrapolation <lgl>, flag_dd_extrapolation <lgl>,
#> #   flag_abandoned <lgl>, flag_reversal <lgl>, flag_poor_fit <lgl>, …
#> 3 species flagged (not counting abandoned habitats or reversals); see summary()
#> Abundances are per site (equal effort in every site and habitat).
nb[c("species", "nb_di", "spillover_abundance", "nb_dd", "flags")]
#> # A tibble: 3 × 5
#>   species                nb_di spillover_abundance  nb_dd flags                 
#>   <chr>                  <dbl>               <dbl>  <dbl> <chr>

#> 2 Scarus schlegeli       0.143                  30 0.399  abandoned, reversal, …
#> 3 Siganus argenteus      0.159                  42 0.0102 abandoned, reversal, …
#> Abundances are per site (equal effort in every site and habitat).
